Multi-Agent Software Defect Prediction

Baseline DeBERTa-v3 + XGBoost Performance & SHAP Explainability Report

Executive Summary: This technical report documents the initial Baseline Model performance and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) feature explainability for Software Defect Prediction (SDP) on the BugHub canonical dataset. Using frozen 768-dimensional representations from microsoft/deberta-v3-small and a regularized XGBoost Classifier on 50,000 stratified issues, the baseline establishes a reliable benchmark of 78.08% Test Accuracy and 0.8235 ROC-AUC with an 86.85% defect detection recall. Further sequence-level LoRA fine-tuning elevated classification accuracy to 84.46% with 0.9048 ROC-AUC.

1. Model Architecture & Setup

ComponentConfigurationMethodological Rationale
Backbone Encodermicrosoft/deberta-v3-small (44M parameters)Disentangled attention capturing deep syntactic and contextual defect patterns.
Embedding Dimension768 dimensions ([CLS] token pooling)Full sequence representation of model_text = title + description.
ClassifierXGBoost (Hist tree method, CUDA accelerated)Non-linear gradient boosted ensembles with native tree-path explainability.
RegularizationL1 reg_alpha=1.0, L2 reg_lambda=3.0, max_depth=6Constrains decision tree depth to mitigate overfitting.
Dataset PartitioningStratified 70% Train (34,999) / 15% Val (7,501) / 15% Test (7,500)Preserves 70.03% Bug / 29.97% Non-Bug class proportions without temporal leakage.

4. SHAP Feature Explainability Analysis

TreeExplainer computed exact Shapley values across 768 latent dimensions for 500 test samples. The top 10 most influential semantic directions separating defects from non-defects are summarized below:

RankLatent DimensionMean |SHAP|Prediction Impact & Semantic Interpretation
1emb_dim_6640.1236Primary defect indicator: High positive values strongly push predictions toward BUG.

4emb_dim_1860.1029Separates code refactoring/enhancement requests from critical defects.
